solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: French chef screws up having left out desserts (11)

indicatorNotes.having left out: to leave something out is to omit it, and here what is left out is L, left

blocks.note: Raymond Blanc, the French chef
screws up = MANGLES, with L (left) taken out

annotation.surface: A famous French chef ruins a batch of puddings by leaving something out.
annotation.walkthrough: L for left is a standard abbreviation. Raymond Blanc runs a celebrated restaurant in Oxfordshire and is a familiar face on British TV.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: these set milk puddings are one kind of dessert.

entries.clue: Take care, shed leaks close to door (3)

indicatorNotes.leaks: something that leaks loses part of its contents, so the shed loses a letter

blocks.note: a byre is a cow shed
the last letter of dooR, the one that leaks away

annotation.surface: A warning to mind the leaky shed near the door.
annotation.walkthrough: BYRE is an old word for a cowshed that crosswords love. Losing the R leaves the farewell.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'take care' is a parting phrase, the same job as a short goodbye.

entries.clue: Stadium regularly painted rear stands (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are taken at even intervals: every second one
indicatorNotes.stands: in a down clue, standing up turns the letters to read bottom to top

blocks.note: every other letter of pAiNtEd ReAr

annotation.surface: The stadium's back stands have been given a coat of paint at regular intervals.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stands" looks like part of the stadium, and here it is the instruction to stand the letters up in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an enclosed ground where crowds watch sport, which is what a stadium is.

entries.clue: Brown rat mainly eaten by animal in caravan? (7)

indicatorNotes.mainly: 'mainly' means for the most part, so most of the word is kept and the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.eaten by: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so RA goes inside the animal

blocks.note: a camel is the animal of a desert caravan
RAT without its last letter

annotation.surface: A brown rat gets swallowed by some beast travelling in a caravan.
annotation.walkthrough: The caravan is a line of camels crossing the desert, not a holiday trailer; the question mark flags that it is an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Colour sense: the golden-brown shade of cooked sugar gives its name to a shade of brown.

entries.clue: Counter-agents stationed in revolutionary state (9)

indicatorNotes.in revolutionary state: letters in a state of revolution are overturned and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Enemy agents have been posted inside a country in the middle of a revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: "Counter-agents" reads as spies working against spies, but it means agents that counter a poison.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: remedies that counteract a poison are agents working against it.

entries.clue: In Winnebago, do things one long awaited (5)

indicatorNotes.In: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: winnebaGO DO Things

annotation.surface: Someone who has waited ages for a trip in a Winnebago motorhome to do some sightseeing.
annotation.walkthrough: Godot is the man who never turns up in Beckett's play Waiting for Godot, so "one long awaited" fits him exactly.
annotation.definitionFit: Allusion: the two tramps in Beckett's play wait the whole time for a man who never arrives.

entries.clue: Designer pen catalogue (7)

blocks.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
a catalogue is a list

annotation.surface: A catalogue of designer pens.
annotation.walkthrough: "Designer pen" reads as a luxury fountain pen, but the pen is a pigsty.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone who designs hair, clothes or interiors.

entries.clue: Ill-mannered individual’s curt sign of contempt (3)

indicatorNotes.curt: curt means cut short, so the word loses its end

blocks.note: the usual word for a lout or oaf
cut short: the final letter is dropped

annotation.surface: A rude person makes a brusque gesture of scorn.
annotation.walkthrough: "Curt" sits naturally beside rudeness, and it is telling you to cut the word short.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the jeer a crowd gives a villain is a noise that shows scorn.

entries.clue: Crime book to need protective covering (9)

blocks.note: B = book
to lack is to need
chain mail, the armour

annotation.surface: A crime novel that needs a protective jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: The protective covering looks like a book cover, and it is armour.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: demanding money with menaces is one criminal offence.

entries.clue: Yet to be paid, striking (11)

blocks.note: a debt still owed stands out on the books
remarkable, standing out from the rest

annotation.surface: A bill still unpaid while the workers are on strike.
annotation.walkthrough: "Striking" sounds like industrial action beside an unpaid bill; here it means remarkable.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses share standing out: an unpaid bill stays standing on the ledger, and a striking thing stands out from others.

entries.clue: Detested suit Charlie leaves packed away (9)

indicatorNotes.leaves: to leave is to depart, so the C departs from the word that follows

blocks.note: a suit is slang for an executive
packed away = CRATED; Charlie (C) leaves it

annotation.surface: A hated suit gets packed away while Charlie walks out.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet. "Suit" is a mildly scornful word for a business executive.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to execrate is to loathe or curse, so the past tense means detested.

entries.clue: Delivery at last bearing winemaker’s must (5)

indicatorNotes.at last: 'at last' means at the very end, so only the word's end, its final letter, is used

blocks.note: the last letter of deliverY
east is a compass bearing

annotation.surface: A shipment of grape must finally arrives at the winery.
annotation.walkthrough: Must is grape juice before fermenting, which is the obvious reading; here "must" means a necessity.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a must is something you cannot do without, and wine cannot ferment without the fungus that turns sugar to alcohol.

entries.clue: Wanting weapon? Bow’s safe (7)

indicatorNotes.Bow’s: Bow is in the East End of London, where a Cockney drops the H

blocks.note: safe = unhurt
as said in Bow, a Cockney district, with the H dropped

annotation.surface: An archer asks whether a bow counts as safe without a weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow reads as the archer's weapon, but it is Bow in London's East End, home of the Cockneys, who drop their aitches.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'wanting' means lacking, and a person lacking arms has no weapon.

entries.clue: Property use wrecked part of building (5,6)

indicatorNotes.wrecked: something wrecked is smashed apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: Misuse of a property has left part of the building in ruins.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface stays in one estate-agent picture, which hides where the fodder ends.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a floor above ground level is one part of a building.

entries.clue: Countryman in street every so often killed maquis (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so HICK sits inside the letters from street
indicatorNotes.every so often: something that happens every so often happens at intervals, so letters are taken at intervals: every second one

blocks.note: every other letter of sTrEeT
a hick is a country bumpkin

annotation.surface: A countryman is killed in the street by the French Resistance.
annotation.walkthrough: The maquis were French Resistance fighters, named after the dense Corsican scrub they hid in; here it is the scrub. "Killed" has no clear job in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: maquis is the dense Mediterranean scrub of Corsica, a tangle of bushes.

entries.clue: Attending Conference maybe leader’s initial form drops (5)

indicatorNotes.Attending: attending means being present beside, so L stands next to PEAR
indicatorNotes.initial: an initial is the first letter of a name, so only the first letter of leader is taken

blocks.note: Conference is a variety of pear
the first letter of Leader

annotation.surface: At the party conference, the leader's first draft falls flat.
annotation.walkthrough: Conference is a common British pear variety, hidden behind a party-conference surface. The answer is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb sense: dew or sweat gathering into little round beads is said to do this, after the gem.

entries.clue: Articles bloke picked up touring Brussels institution (9)

indicatorNotes.picked up: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads upwards
indicatorNotes.touring: a tourer goes round a place, so the reversed MAN goes round EU

blocks.note: the articles A and THE
MAN reversed
Brussels is the seat of the EU

annotation.surface: A man picks up some articles while visiting an institution in Brussels.
annotation.walkthrough: Brussels stands for the European Union. London's Athenaeum is a famous gentlemen's club.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a literary or learned club or library is one kind of institution.

entries.clue: Travelling underground primarily, one arriving in High Barnet? (4,5)

annotation.definition: Travelling underground primarily, one arriving in High Barnet?

indicatorNotes.primarily: 'primarily' means in the first place, so the first letters are taken
indicatorNotes.arriving in: someone arriving in a place ends up inside it, so I goes inside
indicatorNotes.High: high means drunk, so the letters of Barnet stagger into a new order

blocks.note: first letters of Travelling Underground
I (one) goes into BARNET, which is rearranged

annotation.surface: A Northern line passenger heading for High Barnet, the station at the end of the line.
annotation.walkthrough: High Barnet is a real London Underground terminus, so the whole clue also describes the answer; "High" reads as part of the name but means drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: such a train does travel mostly below ground and pulls in at High Barnet, the top of the Northern line.

entries.clue: Bare region no longer covered by crop? (4,5)

annotation.definition: Bare region no longer covered by crop?

blocks.note: the surface suggests bare farmland; it is a bare spot on the scalp
the crop is a crop of hair, not a harvest; the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: A stretch of field left bare now that no crop grows on it.
annotation.walkthrough: The crop reads as a farmer's harvest, but it is a crop of hair.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: the spot on a head where the crop of hair no longer grows.

entries.clue: Alan Shearer missing an odd practice session (9)

indicatorNotes.missing: what is missing is absent, so the letters of AN are taken out
indicatorNotes.odd: something odd is out of the ordinary, so the remaining letters leave their usual order

blocks.note: ALAN SHEARER without A and N

annotation.surface: The former England striker skips an unusual training session.
annotation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a former England football captain, now a TV pundit. "Odd" looks like it describes the session.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the run-through where performers practise before the show.

entries.clue: Who might conduct tests when perhaps on QE2? (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one thing on another sits on top of it, so AS SAY comes above ER

blocks.note: as = when
say = perhaps, for example
Queen Elizabeth II, Elizabeth Regina

annotation.surface: Who carries out tests aboard the liner QE2?
annotation.walkthrough: QE2 reads as the ocean liner Queen Elizabeth 2, but it stands for the queen herself.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to assay is to test a metal or ore for purity, so the one who does it conducts tests.

entries.clue: Indian freezing, without scrap of clothing (5)

indicatorNotes.without: 'without' means lacking, so the word goes on lacking the letter
indicatorNotes.scrap of: a scrap is a tiny piece, so only one letter of clothing is taken

blocks.note: Baltic = bitterly cold
first letter of Clothing, which is dropped

annotation.surface: Someone from India feels the cold without a stitch on.
annotation.walkthrough: "Indian" looks like a person, but it is the food, a British curry-house staple cooked in a wok-like pan. Baltic is informal British for freezing.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one kind of curry dish, so an Indian in the sense of an Indian meal.

entries.clue: Understudy, on reflection, pans upcoming film (3,4)

indicatorNotes.on reflection: a mirror turns the word round
indicatorNotes.upcoming: in a down clue, the word comes up, read bottom to top

blocks.note: a sub is a substitute
pans are pots

annotation.surface: An understudy, thinking it over, gives a bad review to a forthcoming film.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pans" reads as critics slating a film; it means cooking pots.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 1956 Marilyn Monroe comedy of that name is a film.

entries.clue: Where archaeologist would study Carthage is at uni possibly (7)

indicatorNotes.possibly: 'possibly' offers another way things might be, so the letters might be arranged another way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: An archaeology student at university may get to study ancient Carthage.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a long description of a place: the ruins of Carthage lie near Tunis.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the ruins of ancient Carthage stand in this North African country.

entries.clue: Something rolled in gold by émigré, it’s said? (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so DIE sits inside AU

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is rolled in games

annotation.surface: An émigré speaks of something wrapped in gold.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole last part: an émigré leaving the country says goodbye, and in French. "Rolled" suggests a carpet or a cigarette; it is dice.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the French farewell is what someone leaving their country for good would say.

entries.clue: Collection of letters ended with John swapping vowels (7)

indicatorNotes.swapping vowels: to swap is to exchange, so the A and O change places between the two words

blocks.note: past = over, ended
john and bog are both slang for a toilet
PAST BOG with A and O exchanged

annotation.surface: A pile of letters ending with one from John, who has mixed up his vowels.
annotation.walkthrough: John reads as a man's name signing off the letters; it is slang for a toilet, as is bog in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the mail that a person or office receives, taken together.

entries.clue: Sound check that might terminate rally (5)

indicatorNotes.Sound: a sound is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by ear

blocks.note: a brake is a check on movement

annotation.surface: A sound check at a political rally that might bring it to an end.
annotation.walkthrough: The rally reads as a mass meeting or a motor race; it is a tennis rally, and a lost service game ends it.
annotation.definitionFit: Tennis sense: winning a point against serve ends a rally and can take the opponent's service game.

entries.clue: Thin as Oliver on screen? (5)

blocks.note: thin and high, like the sound of a reed instrument
like the actor Oliver Reed, a made-up adjective from his surname

annotation.surface: An actor looking thin on camera.
annotation.walkthrough: Oliver Reed was a burly English film actor, so anything like him on screen is Reed-y; the question mark admits the made-up word.
annotation.definitionFit: A voice like a reed pipe is thin and piping, and the joke sense turns the surname Reed into an adjective.

entries.clue: Ruined relations essentially fixed by international talks (2,7)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a thing is its core, so the middle letter is taken
indicatorNotes.fixed by: the T is fixed into NATTERS

blocks.note: I = international
natters = chatty talks
the middle letter of relaTions

annotation.surface: Relations have broken down and international talks try to repair them.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is diplomacy, but the talks are just chat: to natter is British for to chat idly.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: clothes torn to rags are the literal case, and the phrase extends to plans or relations that are ruined.

entries.clue: National setter? (3)

blocks.note: a national is a newspaper sold across the whole country, here a well-known tabloid
the thing that sets each evening, not a crossword setter

annotation.surface: A setter who works for a national paper.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British national daily newspaper. Setter also suggests the crossword setter.
annotation.definitionFit: A national is a nationwide newspaper, of which this tabloid is one, and the star sets every evening.

entries.clue: Root for Nigerian PM making comeback (3)

indicatorNotes.making comeback: to come back is to return, so the word comes back, read right to left

blocks.note: Theresa May, former British prime minister

annotation.surface: A Nigerian cheers on a prime minister returning to office.
annotation.walkthrough: "Root for" reads as cheer on; here it is a root vegetable, a staple food in Nigeria.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the starchy tuber is a staple of the Nigerian diet.

entries.clue: Trump presented cryptically coarse (5-6)

indicatorNotes.presented: something presented is delivered to an audience, here by voice

blocks.note: to ruff is to trump in cards
the second word says how the card term is delivered

annotation.surface: Trump's words, delivered in a coded way, are vulgar.
annotation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the answer is "ruff" said out loud, and to ruff is to play a trump. The surface points at the politician.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone crude and unpolished in speech is coarse.
